sources.title: ralphex README.md
sources.locator: Features; Quick Start; Phase 1-4; Plan Creation; Usage; Platform Support
sources.finding: Standalone local CLI executes plan checklists, commits each task and runs configurable review stages. Linux/macOS supported; Windows source build is best-effort with missing signal/locking/process-cleanup behavior.

sources.title: ralphex README.md
sources.finding: Optional browser dashboard streams SSE output with phase filters, collapsible sections, text search and late-join full history. Watch mode monitors multiple progress files in a session sidebar. This is monitoring, not established browser control of execution.

sources.title: ralphex docs/custom-providers.md
sources.locator: Codex executor mode; Requirements; Wrapper path
sources.finding: Claude Code is default; native --codex mode needs Codex 0.130.0+. Compatible wrapper scripts support Gemini, Pi, Copilot, OpenCode or custom tools. Native reviews use provider subagent mechanisms; --codex skips external Codex review.

sources.title: ralphex README.md
sources.finding: Optional --worktree runs plans in separate Git worktrees; Docker wrapper mounts project/credentials with documented sandbox limits. Worktrees only apply to full/tasks-only modes.

sources.title: ralphex LICENSE
sources.finding: MIT license covers ralphex source at pinned revision.

sources.title: ralphex v1.7.0 release
sources.finding: Release published 7 September 2026; default-branch changes continue through 7 November.

sources.title: ralphex website
sources.locator: 'Where is ralphex on GitHub?'; footer; '--codex mode' FAQ
sources.finding: Says ralphex is open source under MIT and uses your own Claude or OpenAI plan. The site shows no price.

sources.title: ralphex README
sources.locator: Agent SDK credit note; options table (--preserve-anthropic-api-key); 'License'
sources.finding: Says unattended runs count against your own Anthropic plan's Agent SDK credit pool or API-key billing, or can switch to your OpenAI/codex plan. ralphex itself has no paid tier and is MIT licensed.

sources.title: umputun/ralphex LICENSE (MIT)
sources.finding: The MIT License lets anyone obtain, use, copy and modify the software free of charge.

sources.title: ralphex Antigravity support at v1.7.0
sources.finding: Ralphex v1.7.0 ships agy-as-claude.sh, a configured replacement for Claude Code in task and review phases that translates Antigravity output into Claude stream-json.

sources.title: ralphex: README.md
sources.locator: Platform support; dashboard; Cursor CLI FAQ; pkg/web/templates/base.html and static/styles.css
sources.finding: The primary client is the installed CLI. Linux/macOS are supported; Windows explicitly builds and runs from source on a best-effort basis, without release binaries or maintainer testing. The optional browser monitoring client has viewport metadata and deliberate 768px/640px phone layout rules; the source client inventory has no native iOS/Android application.

sources.title: ralphex: README.md
sources.locator: FAQ Can I use Cursor CLI instead of Claude Code?
sources.finding: The first-party README explicitly documents Cursor CLI as a community-tested drop-in agent: claude_command=agent and claude_args=--force --output-format stream-json. Ralphex launches it through the task/review executor. Compatibility depends on Cursor retaining the expected stream format and is not officially supported.

sources.title: ralphex: cmd/ralphex/main.go
sources.locator: opts Serve/Host/RALPHEX_WEB_HOST; executePlan/buildLogger; pkg/web/server.go; README Docker wrapper
sources.finding: The CLI deliberately serves a network monitoring dashboard using --serve --host or RALPHEX_WEB_HOST. The installed host owns agent execution and the browser is an SSE observer, so a separately deployed operator host/Docker host can continue work with the client laptop disconnected. No Ralphex-operated cloud runtime is implemented in the inspected execution paths.

sources.title: ralphex: README.md
sources.locator: Docker-in-container support and host Docker socket security note
sources.finding: The optional Docker wrapper documents that macOS Docker has VM isolation, in contrast to the Linux host-socket security warning. This is the operator Docker-on-macOS VM boundary, not a per-task Ralphex VM provisioning service.

sources.title: ralphex: pkg/plan/parse.go
sources.locator: Plan, Task, Checkbox, TaskStatus; ParsePlanFile; README Plan Creation; processor task loop
sources.finding: Ralphex creates or imports Markdown plan files independently of an execution session. Task sections and persisted checkboxes are parsed into product task objects and pending/active/done states; users can edit the file, exit after planning, and execute/resume it later. Completed plans are archived. This is a native file-backed task workflow, not an external tracker link or chat-only list.

sources.title: ralphex: pkg/web/server.go
sources.locator: Complete HTTP route registration; static/app.js; cmd/ralphex/main.go; config defaults; processor prompt expansion
sources.finding: The inspected client/runtime route and command surface has terminal-started execution plus a read-only SSE monitoring dashboard, with no inbound scheduled/event execution, human prompt submission via shared sessions, human role/SSO layer or analytics opt-out switch. Dashboard diffStats contains only changed-file/addition/deletion counts, not proposed-code hunks. Review prompts expand reviewer roles into the selected harness native Task/spawn_agent tools; no Ralphex-owned session delegation tool is supplied. The optional finalize prompt rebases/organizes commits without a PR operation.
